subject: Isolated deployment: patch cadence, SBOM export, and third-party validation questionnaire
messages:
From: Michael Summers <michael.summers@medixhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance-team@medixhealth.com

Subject: Isolated deployment: patch cadence, SBOM export, and third-party validation questionnaire

Hi Mina / Aditya,

Thanks for taking this. Medix Health is working through the last tranche of technical controls for our isolated (air-gapped) deployment acceptance. We need a short, focused set of confirmations and artifacts for procurement and our InfoSec team. Please see the items below — if you can respond directly in-thread with attachments or links we can attach to the RFP binder, that would be ideal.

Key questions:
1) Maintenance windows & patch cadence: what is the recommended patch cadence for security-critical CVEs for on-prem air-gapped installs? How do you coordinate emergency (out-of-band) patches with customers who cannot reach external registries?

2) SBOM/Provenance: can you export a machine-readable SBOM for the deployed container images and inference runtime? Preferred formats: CycloneDX or SPDX. Sample export would be helpful.

3) Supply chain validation: do you provide signed releases (GPG/signatures) and reproducible build metadata? How do you validate third-party library provenance (hashes, origin)?

4) Offline patch delivery & verification: what's the mechanism for delivering patches (tarballs, signed artifacts, CRR images)? Are there verification scripts/checksums you provide?

5) Maintenance testing in air-gapped: do you provide a canary/update test plan we can run in our isolated lab prior to org-wide rollouts?

6) Attestation / evidence: can you produce a short attestation template confirming the above items for our auditors? We will attach this to our procurement packet (MH-COMP-2028-09).

Timing: our procurement deadline is 2028-01-20. If you can get initial answers + artifacts by EOD 2028-01-12, we can move forward to the legal/contract step.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Summers
Director, Infrastructure & Compliance
Medix Health
michael.summers@medixhealth.com

Michael — thanks for the clear checklist. Answers below by numbered item; I've attached two artifacts: airgap-maintenance-matrix.xlsx (matrix + recommended cadence) and sbom-export-sample.json (CycloneDX sample from a recent private build).

1) Maintenance windows & patch cadence:
- Recommended cadence: monthly security bundle (non-critical) + immediate (within 72 hours) support for critical CVEs when a signed hotfix is required. For customers who require slower cadences we support scheduled quarterly rollouts.
- Emergency workflow: we publish signed patch artifact packages to a secure SFTP bundle and a signed checksum manifest. Customers pull the bundle via an approved channel (SFTP or airgap USB transfer). For Dedicated customers we can provide signed OCI layers as tar archives.

2) SBOM/Provenance:
- We support CycloneDX and SPDX exports for all release images. The attached sbom-export-sample.json is CycloneDX v1.4 (truncated for the sample).
- SBOM contains package checksums, source repo commit hashes, and build metadata (toolchain versions, build time).

3) Supply chain validation:
- Releases are cryptographically signed (GPG and signing via our build system). We publish the public signing keys to a verification endpoint and include signatures with each artifact.
- Reproducible build metadata: we include a build manifest (git commit, buildkite/CI id, binary hashes) for each release. Third-party library provenance is recorded in the SBOM and cross-referenced with public registries where available.

4) Offline patch delivery & verification:
- Mechanisms: (a) signed tarball of OCI layers + manifest, (b) signed RPM/DEB bundles, (c) USB-deliverable tar + signature for isolated labs.
- Verification scripts: we provide a small bash/python verification tool that consumes the manifest and verifies signatures/hashes locally. Example SHA256 checksums included in the attached matrix reference.

5) Maintenance testing in air-gapped:
- Canary plan: we provide a step-by-step canary test runbook (pre-checks, apply to a single node, smoke tests, rollback steps). We recommend running the canary in an isolated staging cluster that mirrors prod for 24–72 hours.

6) Attestation / evidence:
- We can provide a short attestation template confirming: signed artifacts, SBOM availability, verification tooling, and the maintenance workflow. If you want, we can return a signed DocuSign attestation (see link) once the wording is agreed.

Next steps: Aditya is copied for technical notes and to offer the sample verification script. If this addresses the checklist we can prepare the DocuSign attestation and propose a canary window.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Principal Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Quick tech notes to supplement Mina's reply: 
- SBOM: our pipeline produces CycloneDX v1.4 by default; we can also emit SPDX on request. The SBOM includes component hashes and the image manifest sha256.
- Verification tooling: verification-cli v0.9 (python) will validate signatures against our published pubkey and can be packaged with the airgap bundle. We'll include usage examples in the canary playbook.
- Canary window suggestion: Jan 18–19 (overnight maintenance window) — we can bring a Redwood engineer to run the first canary with your platform team.

I can host a 60-minute technical workshop to walk through the verification CLI and canary steps — propose Jan 13 or Jan 16, 10:00–11:00 PT. Calendar: https://cal.redwood.com/aditya/book
